_note_known_missing_audio: The baseline of registry/known_missing_audio.json, READ by both halves of G-MEDIA (s60_audio._media_gate on the cache, s70_export.media_gate on the notes). That registry excuses a declared audio slot from the only gate that adjudicates it, so its population is pinned here for the same reason known_no_entry_max and wordlist_invalid_max are: adding a row means editing this number in the SAME commit, and a row that DDO repairs means removing the row and bumping this number down. Fail-closed on a missing key, exactly like G-SUPPRESS and G-ADMIT: delete this line and every registry row is over its baseline, so the excuse cannot be granted by deleting the check. 4 = the four slots verified zero-byte upstream on 2026-08-27. Like every other baseline in this file it needs a human signature.
_note_money_gates: The two policy numbers of the money gates (patch plan 2.6), READ by gates.post_wave_gates through gates.read_gates_policy: change a value here and the verdict changes, which test_the_registry_policy_numbers_are_not_dead_data asserts. They were DEAD DATA for one review round -- no caller passed a policy dict, the module constants decided both gates, and editing a file a human had signed changed nothing. G-BILL passes when a wave cost no more than the quote x bill_tolerance_factor. G-CACHE passes when cached == declared on every request that should have been cached, OR sum(cached) / (declared x THE REQUESTS OF THE WAVE THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN CACHED) >= cache_hit_min_share. The denominator is the wave, not the rows that happen to carry a cache name: dividing by the hits made 1 hit + 99 full-price fallbacks score 1.00 and pass. The audit's cached/prompt >= 0.90 criterion is measured WRONG (0.632 at n=20 on a wave whose cache hit 1.00) and must never come back. Both values are the patch plan's; like every other baseline in this file they need a human signature.
_note_think_gate: G-THINK's three POLICY numbers, READ by gates.post_wave_gates through gates.read_gates_policy. They are not measurements: the measurement is the per-kind mean and non-zero share under thinking.THINKING_PER_REQUEST_LOW_BY_KIND in work/probes/stats.json, rebased from the production usage ledger by tools/backfill_probe_stats.py --rebase-thinking-from. These three are the margin a human signs around that measurement. G-THINK passes when, for every request kind in the wave, mean thoughts/request <= max(measured mean x think_mean_margin, think_mean_floor_tokens, measured max / requests) AND the share of rows that thought at all <= max(measured share x think_mean_margin, think_nonzero_share_floor, 1/requests). THE PER-ROW MAXIMUM IS REPORTED AND NEVER FAILED, and that is the whole point of this block. Until 2026-08-27 the gate held every row of a kind in MEASURED_OUTPUT_KINDS to EXACTLY zero thought tokens, because the constant came from 62 probe observations that all happened to be zero and was written down as an absolute. The first real definition wave -- 3,644 paid requests, mean 1.941 tokens/request, p95 0, max 797, 44 rows (1.21%) non-zero, every one finishReason=STOP and healthy -- produced 44 violations, i.e. correct output could not pass the gate. Same disease as G-CACHE's cached/prompt criterion and G-SCRIPT's GB2312 test. The two 'measured max / requests' and '1/requests' terms are the small-wave allowance: one row at the highest value ever measured is the tail that was measured, so it can never fail a wave by itself. Sizing: a wave that accidentally ran at MEDIUM means mean 578.7 tokens/request, which is 58x the floor and 298x the definition wave's measured mean -- two orders of magnitude of headroom, so the margin can be generous without losing the accident it exists to catch. Like every other baseline in this file these need a human signature.
_note_script_gate: G-SCRIPT baselines (patch plan 1.9 / N-05), READ by gates.script_gate_rows through gates.read_gates_policy. Three tiers: BLOCK is any forbidden class on a cell THIS pipeline wrote and has no tolerance; BASELINE is the same class on a 2025 cell (provenance migrated:*) and the pinned count below is its maximum; REVIEW is reported and never fails. Calibrated by running the shipped gate code over all 85,259 cells on disk on 2026-08-26 -- not an ad-hoc script, not by hand. Growing a number here means editing this file in the same commit as whatever grew it, exactly as for G-SUPPRESS and G-ADMIT. SHRINKING is reported and never fails, because the clean retranslation is supposed to take every one of these to zero: it rewrites each cell with gemini:* provenance, which moves the class from BASELINE to BLOCK by itself, with no second edit and nobody having to remember to tighten anything. The 325 Chinese definition cells are Traditional characters mixed into Simplified text (2.41%, 63 entries, 28 of them contaminated in every translated sense); the 20 expression cells are pinyin in the lemma; the 3 Chinese and 1 German cells are the four real defects three audits found by hand (Cyrillic lemma, Arabic gloss, Cyrillic gloss, and a Greek beta written where a German sharp s was meant). greek_in_lemma is NOT pinned here and its count is 0: the two Chinese cells that used to sit in it are the DDO entries `my` and `ny`, whose Chinese lemmas are phrases meaning 'Greek letter M' / 'Greek letter N' and whose glosses explain that same letter. Both the prompt's script contract and the gate now permit a Greek character in a lemma that NAMES the letter when the cell's own gloss mentions it -- entry-subject based, no per-entry whitelist -- and they report it as greek_subject_lemma at REVIEW. Without that, the clean redo had no way to translate those two entries at all: it rewrites them with gemini:* provenance, which moves the class to BLOCK, and the wave would FatalError at ingest with the money already spent. Script leakage is still BLOCK: a lemma that IS the bare Greek letter, or one where the letter is hugged by Latin letters, or one whose gloss never mentions it. Left OUT of this table on purpose: 11 greek_mention cells (three entries whose subject IS a Greek letter), 2 greek_subject_lemma cells and 64 latin_in_han_lemma cells (Chinese cross-references of the form 'see <Danish word>'), all REVIEW. A naive 'any character outside the target script' rule produces 17 FINDINGS on 15 cells here (two Greek-letter cells hit twice, once in the lemma and once in the gloss) and 13 of the 17 are those REVIEW classes -- a 76.5% false-positive rate per finding, 73.3% per cell, and the reason the tiers exist. Like every other baseline in this file these need a human signature. RECALIBRATED 2026-08-27 in the same commit as the two classifier fixes that moved the numbers, per the bump discipline above -- these are SHRINKS, which the gate reports and never fails, and they are pinned down here anyway so the pinned count keeps meaning what the shipped classifier measures. (1) traditional_han is no longer a GB2312-encodability test but a lookup in registry/traditional_variants.json, the characters that HAVE a distinct simplified form. Chinese definitions 325 -> 317, Chinese expressions 22 -> 20: 8 and 2 cells respectively were rare SIMPLIFIED characters the old test could not encode. Re-measured by running the shipped gate code over the same populations it was first calibrated on (13,518 archive definition cells, 8,590 archive expression cells). (2) pinyin_in_lemma now requires a pinyin TONE MARK instead of accepting a bare parenthesis, so it stays at 20 -- all 20 archive expression cells are tone-marked, which is why the count did not move -- and the parenthesis-only population it used to swallow has its own class, foreign_text_in_lemma, pinned NOWHERE because its honest baseline is 0 in both archive kinds. That class is BLOCK: a parenthesised Danish word inside a shipped Chinese lemma is a DDO-text-in-the-deck defect as well as a script one. A fourth class, latin_subject_lemma, is REVIEW and unpinned like its sibling greek_subject_lemma: the entry's subject IS the Latin symbol (the neutral pronoun TA, the cards Q/J/K, solfege do/re/fa/la/sol, F sharp, CD, the letter O-slash), so the lemma has to be able to name it. It takes 18 cells of the new definitions, 6 archive definition cells and 3 archive expression cells out of latin_in_han_lemma, which is left holding exactly the cross-reference population it was described as (55 archive definition cells, 'see <Danish word>').
